title: Relative character tangent weights and canonical centralizer comparisons
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $G$ a group object in schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sc-group-scheme]. Use the split torus $T=\mathbf G_{m,A}^r$ [def-sfb-split-torus-over-ring]. For $i:T\to G$, $m\in\mathbf Z^r$, and every $A$-algebra $B$, put $\chi_m(t)=\prod_jt_j^{m_j}$. The relative tangent module is the existing module $\operatorname{Lie}(G)=\operatorname{Hom}(e^*\Omega_{G/A},\mathcal O_A)$, identified with dual-number points reducing to the identity, using $A[\epsilon]$ [def-sc-dual-numbers], with addition induced by multiplication and scaling by $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$. A tangent vector has weight $m$ if after every algebra extension $B\to C$ and for every $t\in T(C)$, conjugation by $i(t)$ equals scaling its infinitesimal coefficient by $\chi_m(t)$. The weight submodule is equivalently the kernel of $\rho-(v\mapsto v\otimes z^m)$; it is the span of the vectors satisfying this universally quantified condition. For a subgroup map $h:H\to G$, its tangent image is the submodule spanned by tangent points obtained by composition with $h$. A module is locally free of rank one when for each prime $p$ some $a\notin p$ gives $V_a\simeq A_a$ using [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. For $k:K\to G$, its centralizer points over $B$ are those commuting with every $K(C)$ point after every $B\to C$. Scalar extension of groups is the pullback along spectra. A Lie comparison $e:B\otimes_A\operatorname{Lie}(G)\to\operatorname{Lie}(G_B)$ is characterized on $b\otimes v$ by the dual-number point obtained by extending $v$ to $B$ and scaling $\epsilon$ by $b$, after the pullback projection to $G$. Successive comparisons for $A\to B\to C$ agree with the direct comparison on $c\otimes(b\otimes v)$ and $c\,h(b)\otimes v$, after the canonical iterated pullback projections.
